summary: Solar Sentry is a browser game that puts players in charge of a lunar orbiter. Players choose an instrument, orbit, launcher, power system, communications hardware and duty cycle, then simulate the mission from design review to data return. The game shows where a design fails and lets players revise it. NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter instrument guide informs the science goals, while a simplified model makes the trade-offs between cost, launch mass, eclipse power and downlink easy to explore.
details:
Players select one of three lunar science objectives and configure a spacecraft. The simulator checks the budget and launch mass, models available power during eclipse, then calculates how much science data can be sent to Earth.

For example, the default laser altimeter mission stalls during eclipse. Changing to a protected duty cycle makes the same spacecraft viable and returns four of four collected science units. NASA’s LRO instrument guide informs the laser altimetry, thermal mapping and imaging objectives. The numerical assumptions are illustrative and are not NASA flight data.

The game runs in a modern browser from index.html and was built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript. ChatGPT assisted with ideation, code, project text and the four-slide demonstration.
